entities.summary:
The Seventh-day Adventist Church is a Protestant Christian denomination headquartered in Silver Spring, Maryland. Founded on October 22, 1863, by Joseph Bates and a group of thirty-seven individuals, the church aimed to revive the Sabbath day as observed in the Bible. Its early emphasis on health reform, biblical literalism, and eschatological teachings drew both criticism and converts.

The Adventist Church has grown to become one of the largest Christian denominations globally, with over 21 million members across more than 200 countries. It operates a significant presence in education, healthcare, and social service, particularly in developing nations. The church's leadership is currently held by Ted Wilson.

As a global institution, the Seventh-day Adventist Church has played a role in shaping Christian thought on Sabbath observance, health reform, and end-times prophecy. Its influence extends into various fields of study and practice, including biblical studies, theology, and education.

With its headquarters established in Silver Spring, Maryland, the church remains committed to spreading its message and values worldwide.
